title: EvalSafetyGap: A Hybrid Survey and Conceptual Framework for LLM Evaluation-Safety Failures

bias_targets.methodology: Synthesizing literature on how pairwise LLM judgments systematically change based on the order in which answers are presented to the evaluator model.
Reviewing literature to demonstrate how LLM judges artificially inflate scores for longer responses, independent of substantive content quality.
Evaluating studies showing that LLM judges exhibit systematic preferences for specific presentation formats, such as Markdown formatting and bulleted lists, while holding content fixed.
Reviewing literature on how LLM evaluators favor outputs generated by their own or related model families, or outputs matching their specific instruction-tuned style.
Aggregating public safety reports and independent evaluations across a 10-model audit to measure models' tendency to agree with user premises or preferences despite contrary evidence.

Briefly referencing adjacent literature (e.g., StereoSet, BBQ) to note how demographic framing and elicitation choices can affect model-mediated judgments, though not empirically measured in the paper's own audit.
